boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Simmons University
boards.description: Ten currently documented food stops with late hours in Boston, including options in Fenway, Back Bay, and nearby college corridors.

cards.title: Tasty Burger Fenway
cards.subtitle: 86 Van Ness Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Use the Fenway location page to confirm the 2:00 a.m. daily closing time before heading over; it lists the address and phone number.
cards.short_summary: A Fenway burger counter with late daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Tasty Burger lists its Fenway location at 86 Van Ness Street as open daily from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily hours of 11:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m.

cards.title: The Halal Guys on Boylston
cards.subtitle: 1260 Boylston Street, Fenway
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s location page for the day-specific closing time; weekdays end at midnight and Friday–Saturday run later.
cards.short_summary: Halal platters and sandwiches with midnight or later service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Halal Guys lists 1260 Boylston Street open until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 1:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: The Halal Guys — Boston, 1260 Boylston Street
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 10:30 a.m.–12:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 a.m.–1:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Crispy Dough Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 1514 Tremont Street, Mission Hill
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s ordering page to verify the current takeout schedule; its listed weekday hours extend to 1:00 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Mission Hill pizza and takeout option with late posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Crispy Dough Pizzeria lists takeout hours until 1:00 a.m. Monday–Thursday, with later Friday and Sunday-night hours.
cards.access_notes: Official ordering page lists takeout until 1:00 a.m. Monday–Thursday, 2:30 a.m. Friday, and 2:30 a.m. Sunday night.

cards.title: Domino's on Park Drive
cards.subtitle: 508 Park Drive, Fenway
cards.notes: Confirm the store’s live hours through the official Boston locator before placing a pickup or delivery order from the Park Drive location.
cards.short_summary: A Park Drive pizza option listed until 2:00 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official Boston locator lists its 508 Park Drive store as open until 2:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official Boston location page displays 508 Park Drive as open until 2:00 a.m.; verify live ordering availability.

cards.title: Raising Cane's on Boylston
cards.subtitle: 755 Boylston Street, Back Bay
cards.notes: The official location page provides a seven-day midnight close; check it again for holiday changes before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: Chicken-finger meals served until midnight every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane’s lists its 755 Boylston Street restaurant open from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant and dine-in hours as 10:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m. Sunday–Saturday.

cards.title: OTTO Pizza near BU
cards.subtitle: 888 Commonwealth Avenue, Boston
cards.notes: Plan around the official schedule: this Commonwealth Avenue counter lists midnight closing on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Pizza by the slice or pie with selected midnight hours.
cards.evidence_claim: OTTO’s 888 Commonwealth Avenue location lists hours until 12:00 a.m. on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 11:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; takeout and delivery orders stop 15 minutes before close.

cards.title: Pinocchio's Pizza & Subs
cards.subtitle: 74 Winthrop Street, Harvard Square
cards.notes: Check the posted academic-year note when planning a weekend pickup; Friday and Saturday service is listed later while students are in session.
cards.short_summary: Harvard Square pizza and subs with an academic-year late schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Pinocchio’s lists hours until 1:00 a.m. Monday–Saturday, and until 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday when students are in session from September through May.
cards.access_notes: Official hours page lists Monday–Saturday until 1:00 a.m.; it states Friday–Saturday extend to 2:00 a.m. during September–May student sessions.

cards.title: Bova's Bakery
cards.subtitle: 134 Salem Street, North End
cards.notes: For an overnight bakery stop, use the official bakery page for the address and its stated around-the-clock schedule.
cards.short_summary: A North End bakery that states it is open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Bova’s Bakery states that it is open 24 hours a day, every day, at 134 Salem Street in Boston’s North End.
cards.access_notes: Official bakery page states it is open 24 hours a day, every day.

cards.title: South Street Diner
cards.subtitle: 178 Kneeland Street, Boston
cards.notes: Use the diner’s late-night page for the exact address and its 24/7 statement; breakfast and dinner are listed as available all night.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 diner serving breakfast and dinner overnight.
cards.evidence_claim: South Street Diner states it is open 24/7 and lists breakfast and dinner served all night at 178 Kneeland Street.
cards.source_title: South Street Diner — Late Night Eats
cards.access_notes: Official late-night page says the diner is open at midnight through 6:00 a.m. and states: open 24/7.

cards.title: Tasty Burger Back Bay
cards.subtitle: 145 Dartmouth Street, Back Bay
cards.notes: Use the Back Bay location page for day-specific hours; Friday and Saturday are the latest listed nights at this Dartmouth Street counter.
cards.short_summary: A Back Bay burger location that reaches 2:00 a.m. on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Tasty Burger lists its Back Bay location at 145 Dartmouth Street open until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Tasty Burger — Back Bay Hours + Location
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 11:00 a.m.–12:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11:00 a.m.–2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Simmons spaces for collaborative work, creative projects, recreation, media-making, and focused study.

cards.title: Make something at the Makerspace
cards.subtitle: One Palace Road, first floor
cards.notes: Check the Makerspace schedule, then use a drop-in hour or extracurricular event to try its 3D printer, Cricut, VR gear, or craft tools.
cards.short_summary: A student-led creative facility for hands-on projects and community participation.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes the Makerspace as a student-led facility with creative and technology equipment; all Simmons community members are invited to extracurricular events and drop-in hours.
cards.access_notes: Simmons says all members of its community are invited to extracurricular events and drop-in hours; check the current schedule.

cards.title: Build a media project at Latz and Cohen
cards.subtitle: Main College Building, first floor
cards.notes: Use this named media hub as a starting point for a campus audio, video, or podcast project; confirm room availability before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named media facility within Simmons’ student-driven media spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons lists the Latz and Cohen Media Center among the student-driven media spaces in the Main College Building.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main College Building’s first floor; confirm applicable access and booking arrangements with Simmons.

cards.title: See where Simmons radio is made
cards.subtitle: Main College Building, first floor
cards.notes: Add the Simmons Radio Station to a media-project walk-through, and ask the relevant program or student group about opportunities and access.
cards.short_summary: A named campus radio space housed with Simmons’ media facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons identifies the Simmons Radio Station as part of its student-driven media spaces in the Main College Building.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main College Building’s first floor; ask Simmons staff or the relevant student media group about access.

cards.title: Plan a shoot at the Alden Trust Video Studio
cards.subtitle: Main College Building, first floor
cards.notes: If a class or organization needs video production space, ask the relevant Simmons media contact about using this named studio and its current setup.
cards.short_summary: A named video-production studio in the student-driven media area.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons lists the Alden Trust Video Studio among its student-driven media spaces in the Main College Building.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Main College Building’s first floor; confirm access and any production policies before planning a session.

cards.entity_name: Jennifer Eckert Center for Leadership and Engagement
cards.title: Meet collaborators at the Eckert Center
cards.subtitle: Drinan Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Use the Jennifer Eckert Center as a check-in point when organizing with a student group or looking for a campus collaboration space.
cards.short_summary: An undergraduate hub for student organizations and collaborative teamwork.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons calls the Jennifer Eckert Center for Leadership and Engagement a vibrant undergraduate hub for student organizations and collaborative teamwork.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Drinan Hall; confirm programming and room-use details with the Center.

cards.title: Take a between-class break at the Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Main College Building A-075; home of the REEF Support Center
cards.notes: Bring coursework or a meal between classes: the lounge has tables, couches, a commuter fridge, microwave, tea kettle, games, and supplies.
cards.short_summary: A work-and-reset space for commuters and Dix Scholars, with REEF Support Center services.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons says the Commuter Student/Dix Scholar Lounge has work tables and lounge seating, food-storage and heating appliances, games, supplies, occasional snacks, and programming.
cards.access_notes: On the Main College Building ground level in A-075; Simmons specifically directs commuters and Dix Scholars to visit.

cards.title: Move between classes at Holmes
cards.subtitle: 331 Brookline Avenue
cards.notes: Check recreation access and schedules, then head to Holmes for the pool, cardio equipment, hardwood courts, or other listed activity areas.
cards.short_summary: Simmons’ recreation center with fitness, court, and pool facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons says the 60,000-square-foot Holmes Sports Center includes a swimming pool, cardio equipment, and hardwood courts for students and members.
cards.access_notes: Simmons lists the facility at 331 Brookline Avenue and says it serves students and members; confirm current recreation access.

cards.entity_name: Simmons University Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve a library room for a group session
cards.subtitle: Simmons University Library, Lefavour Hall
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room in advance for a project meeting, presentation rehearsal, or shared work block; bookings are offered in three-hour blocks.
cards.short_summary: Twenty reservable library rooms for group work of up to eight people.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simmons University Library has 20 group study rooms for student use, each accommodating up to eight people and reservable in three-hour blocks.
cards.source_title: Rooms and Spaces | Simmons University Library
cards.access_notes: Student rooms may be reserved up to 28 days ahead through the Library Study Room Reservations system; booking ahead is recommended.

cards.title: Choose the Low-Sensory Study Room
cards.subtitle: Simmons University Library, Lefavour Hall
cards.notes: When you need fewer distractions, reserve this room and plan a quiet individual study block around its reduced-light environment.
cards.short_summary: A reservable library room designed for students with different sensory preferences.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons designates the Low-Sensory Study Room for different sensory preferences and says it has reduced lighting designed to minimize distraction.
cards.source_title: Rooms and Spaces | Simmons University Library
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the library’s Low Sensory Study Room reservation link; confirm availability before visiting.

cards.title: Settle into the 24-Hour Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, first floor, E-101
cards.notes: Use this ultra-quiet room for focused individual work when other library spaces are busy; bring your Simmons ID for entry.
cards.short_summary: An ID-access study room dedicated to ultra-quiet work around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons says its 24-Hour Silent Study Room is open daily to Simmons University ID holders and intended for ultra-quiet work.
cards.source_title: Rooms and Spaces | Simmons University Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists E-101 in Lefavour Hall as open 24 hours a day, seven days a week; Simmons University ID is required.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost places and activities for Simmons students and the public in Boston.

cards.title: See the MFA with your Simmons ID
cards.subtitle: 465 Huntington Avenue, beside the academic campus
cards.notes: Bring your current Simmons ID to the admissions desk, then spend time together in the collection galleries without buying a general-admission ticket.
cards.short_summary: Simmons ID holders receive free MFA admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons University states that students can show a Simmons ID for free admission at the Museum of Fine Arts.
cards.source_title: The Official Simmons Guide to Boston
cards.access_notes: Simmons ID required; the university page describes free admission.

cards.title: Walk the Gardner galleries
cards.subtitle: 25 Evans Way, next to Simmons' academic campus
cards.notes: Show a current Simmons ID for admission, then take a slow gallery-and-courtyard visit with friends; check the museum’s visitor rules before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A Simmons ID unlocks a no-cost museum visit next door.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons University states that students can show a Simmons ID for free admission at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum.
cards.source_title: The Official Simmons Guide to Boston
cards.access_notes: Simmons ID required; the university page describes free admission.

cards.title: Browse MassArt Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 621 Huntington Avenue, near Simmons
cards.notes: Meet at MAAM to view its contemporary-art exhibitions, then use the museum’s visitor information to plan around the current open days.
cards.short_summary: A nearby contemporary-art museum with always-free entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons University identifies MassArt Art Museum as always free.
cards.source_title: The Official Simmons Guide to Boston
cards.access_notes: The Simmons guide states that MAAM is always free; consult the museum for current visiting hours.

cards.title: Meet beneath “Free to All”
cards.subtitle: 700 Boylston Street, Copley Square
cards.notes: Use the Central Library as a no-purchase meetup for reading, conversation, or a self-guided look at its public spaces and collections.
cards.short_summary: Boston’s central library explicitly welcomes everyone under its free-to-all commitment.
cards.evidence_claim: Boston Public Library says its commitment to be “Free to All” welcomes everyone equally.
cards.access_notes: Public library access; bring ID only if a specific service requires it.

cards.title: Cross the river for free galleries
cards.subtitle: 32 Quincy Street, Cambridge
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit with friends on a Tuesday-through-Sunday opening day; admission is free, so there is no need to buy a museum ticket.
cards.short_summary: Free public access to Harvard’s art collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard University states that Harvard Art Museums are free and open to all visitors Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Free public admission Tuesday through Sunday; confirm current hours before travel.

cards.title: See contemporary art at the List
cards.subtitle: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street, Cambridge
cards.notes: Gather for a contemporary-art gallery visit at the List Center; its galleries and programs are open to the public without an admission charge.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s List Center offers no-cost public galleries and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List Visual Arts Center states that its galleries and all programs are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: About the MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; check the center for current gallery hours.

cards.entity_name: Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East
cards.title: Explore the Ancient Near East museum
cards.subtitle: 6 Divinity Avenue, Cambridge
cards.notes: Choose a Sunday-through-Friday visit and explore the museum’s objects and displays together; public admission does not require a ticket purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission Harvard museum focused on the ancient Near East.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard University states that the Harvard Museum of the Ancient Near East is open to the public and free of admission Sunday through Friday.
cards.access_notes: Free public admission Sunday through Friday; confirm current hours before travel.

cards.title: Take a plant-collection walk
cards.subtitle: 125 Arborway, Jamaica Plain
cards.notes: Pick a route through the living collections and walk it at your own pace with friends; daily entry is free for everyone to explore.
cards.short_summary: A large public landscape of documented plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvard University states that the 281-acre Arnold Arboretum is open daily and free for all to explore.
cards.access_notes: Open daily and free for all to explore; follow Arboretum visitor guidance.

cards.title: Start at the Shattuck Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: 125 The Fenway, in the Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Stop in for park context, an exhibit, and a free map, then use the information to shape a walk through the nearby Emerald Necklace.
cards.short_summary: A public Back Bay Fens visitor center with free maps and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Emerald Necklace Conservancy says the Shattuck Visitor Center offers free maps and free things to do, including exhibits.
cards.access_notes: Visitor center hours vary by season; its free map and exhibits do not require a purchase.

cards.title: Join a Back Bay Fens walking tour
cards.subtitle: Tours begin at Shattuck Visitor Center in the Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Register for a Conservancy docent-led public walk to explore the park’s landscape and history; a donation is suggested, not required.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost guided walk through the Emerald Necklace, with an optional donation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Emerald Necklace Conservancy states that its guided walking tours are free, with a suggested $10 donation.
cards.access_notes: Tours run May through October; registration and cancellation details are posted by the Conservancy. Suggested donation is optional.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named Simmons study environments in Lefavour Hall, with library and map documentation for location or reservation/access details.

cards.title: Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, first floor, E-101
cards.notes: Bring your Simmons ID and set up for independent work in E-101. The library lists this as its silent room and says it is open around the clock.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated 24/7 quiet room for individual focus.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons Library lists the Silent Study Room in Lefavour Hall E-101 as open 24 hours, seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Hours and Location | Simmons University Library
cards.access_notes: Library identifies the room as Lefavour Hall, first floor, E-101, open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

cards.title: Beatley Library
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Use the library’s tables, carrels, seating, research materials, and librarian support as a flexible base for reading, writing, or research sessions.
cards.short_summary: The central library setting for research and a range of work styles.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes its University Library as a student resource hub and documents library study spaces in Lefavour Hall.
cards.access_notes: Located at 300 The Fenway in Lefavour Hall; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: First-Floor Lounge Seating
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Choose this map-listed lounge seating when you want a softer, open setting. Keep your materials contained so the shared seating remains usable.
cards.short_summary: A casual seating zone on the library’s first floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies lounge seating on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: Map-listed in Lefavour Hall. Check building and library access conditions before arrival.

cards.title: First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve ahead for a structured group work session. The library’s reservation guidance covers group study rooms for two to six students in three-hour blocks.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for small collaborative sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lefavour Hall study map lists first-floor study rooms, and Simmons states library group rooms are reservable for two to six students.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the Library Study Room Reservations system; rooms may be booked in three-hour blocks up to 28 days ahead.

cards.title: Second-Floor Conference Room
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, second floor
cards.notes: Locate this map-listed conference room for planned collaborative work. Confirm reservation requirements before relying on it for a meeting or presentation practice.
cards.short_summary: A designated second-floor conference setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies a conference room on the second floor and marks it as requiring advance reservation.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: The map marks conference rooms with double asterisks, indicating that they must be reserved ahead of time.

cards.entity_name: Lefavour Hall Second-Floor Private Study/Meeting Room
cards.title: Private Study/Meeting Room
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, second floor
cards.notes: Plan a focused one-to-one or small meeting here, then reserve before you go. It is specifically labeled as a private study/meeting room on the map.
cards.short_summary: A map-designated private room for study or meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies a private study/meeting room on the second floor and marks it for advance reservation.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: The map’s double-asterisk key says this room must be reserved ahead of time.

cards.title: Third-Floor Study Cubicles
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Take a cubicle for a defined individual workstation. Use headphones and leave the space clear when you finish so another student can use it.
cards.short_summary: Individual workstations on the library’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies study cubicles on the third floor.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: Map-listed in Lefavour Hall; check library and building access conditions before arrival.

cards.entity_name: Lefavour Hall Third-Floor Library Reading Room
cards.title: Third-Floor Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Use this named reading room for a library-centered study session. Pair it with library search or research help when your work needs scholarly sources.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading-room environment within Lefavour Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies a Library Reading Room on the third floor.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: Map-listed in Lefavour Hall; consult current library hours and access guidance before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Lefavour Hall Fourth-Floor Terrace Lounge Seating
cards.title: Fourth-Floor Terrace Lounge Seating
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, fourth floor terrace
cards.notes: Head to this named terrace lounge seating when an open shared setting suits your task. Check on-site conditions and keep weather-sensitive work protected.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor terrace seating area shown on the study map.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies terrace lounge seating on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: Map-listed in Lefavour Hall. Availability and building access may vary.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lefavour Hall, fourth floor
cards.notes: Book a room in advance for a small group task, shared screen work, or a focused project check-in. Bring your reservation details with you.
cards.short_summary: Upper-floor reservable rooms for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ Lefavour Hall study map identifies study rooms on the fourth floor and marks them for advance reservation.
cards.source_title: Study Map Key for Lefavour Hall
cards.access_notes: The map marks study rooms with double asterisks, indicating advance reservation is required.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named cultural and park destinations along Huntington Avenue, The Fenway, and Massachusetts Avenue beside Simmons University.

cards.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
cards.subtitle: Huntington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from Huntington Avenue and use the museum’s current visit page to choose galleries, a program, or a timed admission option before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A museum stop with galleries, programs, and a clearly identified Huntington Avenue entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The MFA identifies 465 Huntington Avenue as its address and the Huntington Avenue Entrance as its main entrance.
cards.source_title: Getting Here | Museum of Fine Arts Boston
cards.access_notes: Current general-admission details and hours are published on the museum’s visit page; admission is ticketed for most visitors.

cards.title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
cards.subtitle: Evans Way beside Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Use Evans Way as the landmark, then reserve a timed ticket if needed; the museum’s directions page lists the Longwood Medical Area stop as a short walk.
cards.short_summary: A named museum destination on Evans Way with official transit and ticket-planning guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gardner Museum lists its address as 25 Evans Way and directs visitors to reserve a ticket time.
cards.source_title: Directions and Parking | Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
cards.access_notes: Advanced ticketing is recommended; the official directions page identifies nearby transit and bike-rack access.

cards.title: MassArt Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Huntington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the museum’s exhibition and visit information, then cross to the 621 Huntington Avenue entrance from the Longwood Medical Area Green Line stop.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art museum directly across from the Longwood Medical Area station.
cards.evidence_claim: MAAM states that it is at 621 Huntington Avenue, directly across the street from the Longwood Medical Area station, and its homepage says it is always free.
cards.access_notes: Review the museum’s posted hours and reserve a free ticket when required; indoor programming may vary by season.

cards.title: Kelleher Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: The Fenway corridor, Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths and fountain from The Fenway side, and check the Conservancy’s seasonal opening dates before planning a flower-focused visit.
cards.short_summary: A formal rose garden and fountain in the Back Bay Fens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Emerald Necklace Conservancy identifies the Kelleher Rose Garden in the Back Bay Fens and lists its seasonal hours.
cards.source_title: Back Bay Fens | The Emerald Necklace Conservancy
cards.access_notes: The Conservancy lists the garden as open April 1–November 1, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; verify conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Fenway Victory Gardens
cards.subtitle: The Fenway corridor, Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Follow the Fens paths toward the garden plots and view them from public walkways; treat the working beds as a community garden rather than a picking area.
cards.short_summary: Historic community garden plots within the Back Bay Fens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Conservancy describes the Victory Gardens as the oldest remaining wartime garden planted in 1941 and a community garden today.
cards.source_title: Back Bay Fens | The Emerald Necklace Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Use public park paths and respect individual garden plots and posted site rules.

cards.title: Japanese Temple Bell
cards.subtitle: The Fenway corridor, Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Use the Back Bay Fens map and park paths to locate the bell, then pause for its documented history as a twentieth-century peace gesture.
cards.short_summary: A 17th-century Japanese temple bell installed in the Fens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Emerald Necklace Conservancy identifies a 17th-century Japanese Temple Bell among the features of the Back Bay Fens.
cards.source_title: Back Bay Fens | The Emerald Necklace Conservancy
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor park feature; access follows public park conditions and any posted restrictions.

cards.title: Shattuck Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: The Fenway corridor, Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Start here when you want a park map or orientation, using the named visitor center at 125 The Fenway as a clear Fens meeting point.
cards.short_summary: The Back Bay Fens visitor-center stop at a former Richardson pump station.
cards.evidence_claim: The Conservancy says the Shattuck Visitor Center in the Back Bay Fens serves as a visitor stop and provides its address as 125 The Fenway.
cards.source_title: Guided Tours | The Emerald Necklace Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Consult the Conservancy’s current tour and visitor-center information before relying on staffed services.

cards.title: Roberto Clemente Field
cards.subtitle: The Fenway corridor, Back Bay Fens
cards.notes: Bring a ball or simply pass the field on a Fens walk; the Conservancy specifically names this track-and-field area among the park’s active recreation spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic-field landmark within the Back Bay Fens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Conservancy lists Clemente Field and describes the Back Bay Fens as including ball fields and active recreation.
cards.source_title: Back Bay Fens | The Emerald Necklace Conservancy
cards.access_notes: Field access and organized use can depend on reservations and posted park rules; use surrounding public paths when facilities are occupied.

cards.title: Jordan Hall
cards.subtitle: Gainsborough Street beside Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Check New England Conservatory’s performance calendar, then use the street entrance at 30 Gainsborough Street for a clearly marked concert-hall destination.
cards.short_summary: A New England Conservatory performance venue with a Gainsborough Street entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: New England Conservatory states that Jordan Hall is in its Jordan Hall building, with a street entrance at 30 Gainsborough Street.
cards.access_notes: Building hours and event access vary; NEC lists academic-year building hours of 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. and publishes concert information separately.

cards.title: Mapparium
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue corridor, Christian Science Plaza
cards.notes: Plan this as an indoor globe-and-exhibit stop at Christian Science Plaza, and use the official experience information to confirm tour availability before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A documented Mapparium globe within the public Christian Science Plaza experience.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mother Church identifies the public How Do You See the World? experience at Christian Science Plaza as including the Mapparium globe.
cards.source_title: The Mother Church in Boston | Christian Science
cards.access_notes: The experience is open to the local Boston community; confirm current exhibit and tour arrangements through the official site before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Simmons University traditions, from century-old spring rituals to annual community celebrations.

cards.title: May Day
cards.subtitle: Simmons’ century-old spring celebration
cards.notes: Look for the spring program and join the community celebration; Simmons identifies May Day as its oldest continuous tradition.
cards.short_summary: A Simmons tradition since 1912 that brings students together each spring.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that May Day is its oldest continuous tradition and describes flower crowns, strawberry-themed brunch, singing, and a maypole dance.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and participation details vary by year; check Simmons announcements.

cards.title: The Maypole Dance
cards.subtitle: A May Day performance tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the ribbon-weaving performance during May Day; Simmons documents the dance as an iconic part of its celebration.
cards.short_summary: Dancers circle and weave streamers around the Maypole during Simmons’ May Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons reports that the Maypole dance is an iconic performance tradition at its May Day and is usually performed by the Simmons University Dance Company.
cards.source_title: Simmons' 2023 May Day Ushers in Spring with Spirit of Inclusivity | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of May Day; confirm the current year’s event schedule.

cards.title: Strawberry Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A May Day food tradition
cards.notes: Check the May Day schedule for the breakfast gathering; archival and university accounts connect strawberry shortcake with the event.
cards.short_summary: A strawberry-centered breakfast tradition within Simmons’ May Day celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that its original 1912 May Day festivities included a strawberry shortcake breakfast and that contemporary May Day begins with a complimentary breakfast.
cards.source_title: Simmons' 2023 May Day Ushers in Spring with Spirit of Inclusivity | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Offered only as part of the annual May Day program; confirm current details with Simmons.

cards.title: Winter Wonderland
cards.subtitle: Residence-hall holiday celebration
cards.notes: Watch for residence-hall decorating and themed activities during the winter program, which Simmons says grew from Olde English Dinner.
cards.short_summary: A winter tradition built around residence-hall decorating, themed dinners, and first-year hosting.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes Winter Wonderland as a tradition with residence-hall decorating, themed dinners, and an ugly sweater party hosted by first-year students.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal programming; consult current Residential Life or Student Affairs announcements.

cards.title: Shark Week
cards.subtitle: Seven days of Simmons spirit
cards.notes: Follow the announced calendar for the week’s activities; Simmons frames Shark Week as a campus-pride tradition evolved from Track Day.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong Simmons spirit program with changing activities and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes Shark Week as seven days of Shark pride and states that it evolved from a tradition originally called Track Day.
cards.access_notes: Activities vary by year; check the current Simmons event schedule.

cards.title: Founder's Day
cards.subtitle: John Simmons’ October 30 birthday
cards.notes: Look for the annual October 30 observance, including the essay contest and community refreshments described by Simmons.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus observance of founder John Simmons’ birthday.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that it celebrates founder John Simmons’ October 30 birthday every year with an essay contest, sparkling apple cider, and cake.
cards.access_notes: Annual October 30 event; confirm the current program with Simmons.

cards.title: Friends and Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: A campus visit tradition with 1960s roots
cards.notes: Use the annual program to plan a visit with invited guests; Simmons traces the tradition to Father-Daughter Weekend in the 1960s.
cards.short_summary: A yearly opportunity for students’ friends and families to experience Simmons.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that Friends and Family Weekend is held every year and began as Father-Daughter Weekend in the 1960s.
cards.access_notes: Annual dates and registration requirements vary; consult Simmons’ current event information.

cards.title: Candle Lighting Ceremony
cards.subtitle: First-year students’ first-night reflection
cards.notes: Attend if invited during first-year arrival programming; Simmons describes it as a first-night pause for reflection and connection.
cards.short_summary: A newer first-year ritual centered on reflection and shared arrival.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes the Candle Lighting Ceremony as a tradition bringing first-year students together on their first night to pause and reflect.
cards.access_notes: Part of first-year programming; availability is limited to the applicable orientation period.

cards.title: Simmons Soiree
cards.subtitle: An annual night of dining and dancing
cards.notes: Check the announced venue, tickets, and guest rules before planning; Simmons presents this newer event as a formal social evening.
cards.short_summary: A formal Simmons social tradition centered on dinner and dancing in Boston.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes the Simmons Soiree as a newer tradition where students and dates spend an evening dining and dancing at Boston venues.
cards.access_notes: Venue, admission, and guest policies vary by year; consult the current Simmons announcement.

cards.title: The Class-Color Convocation Procession
cards.subtitle: First-years process in wearing their class color
cards.notes: Wear the class color specified in orientation communications and join the Convocation procession when scheduled for your entering class.
cards.short_summary: A Convocation entrance ritual in which the first-year class wears its designated color.
cards.evidence_claim: A Simmons fall-orientation program states that the first-year class processes into University Convocation wearing its class color.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during University Convocation; class-color and lineup instructions are provided by Simmons.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Simmons University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on campus, connecting with student life, and exploring nearby arts spaces.

cards.title: Start with the Academic Quad
cards.subtitle: First stop — Main College Building, 300 The Fenway
cards.notes: Begin outside the Main College Building and use the academic quad as your landmark while you identify entrances, campus services, and routes between buildings.
cards.short_summary: Use the academic-campus hub to get your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons identifies 300 The Fenway as its Boston campus address and depicts the Main College Building on its campus map.
cards.source_title: Campus Tours and Information Sessions | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor orientation stop; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Set a Meet-Up Point at Common Grounds
cards.subtitle: Second stop — College Center, Main College Building
cards.notes: Choose a simple meeting point in Common Grounds, then use the nearby student computers and wireless area to coordinate the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus café stop with seating and nearby student resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that Common Grounds Cafe is in the College Center of the Main College Building and that its surrounding area has computers and free wireless access for students.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks are sold; confirm current hours and payment options before going.

cards.title: Reserve a Library Study Room
cards.subtitle: Third stop — University Library, 300 The Fenway
cards.notes: Book a group study room for a short planning session, browse the library spaces, and save the research-help links for your first assignments.
cards.short_summary: Turn a short library visit into a practical study-plan setup.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simmons University Library offers 20 group study rooms for student use, reservable up to 28 days ahead.
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations and library access may require a Simmons account or ID.

cards.title: Find a Piece of Simmons History
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop — University Archives at the Library
cards.notes: Pause at the Archives exhibit in Lefavour Hall, then note one campus-history topic to revisit when you want context beyond the current semester.
cards.short_summary: Pair campus orientation with an archival history stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons University Library lists a University Archives exhibit on gender equality and LGBTQIA+ activism in Lefavour Hall, Level 1.
cards.access_notes: Exhibit availability can change; check with the library service desk if needed.

cards.title: See What Is Hanging at Trustman
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop — Main College Building, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and take a quiet gallery lap; return for an artist talk or opening if the calendar lists one that fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery visit that works as a calm afternoon reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Trustman Art Gallery is in the Main College Building’s fourth floor and presents professional artists’ work plus an annual student exhibition.
cards.source_title: About the Trustman Gallery | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours listed by Simmons are Monday–Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m., Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; verify exhibition dates before visiting.

cards.title: Locate a Backup Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop — One Palace Road, Academic Campus
cards.notes: Use the building’s study map to find the lobby lounge and identify reservable private rooms, giving your group a backup place for a later work session.
cards.short_summary: Know where to go when you need a quieter campus base.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ One Palace Road study map identifies a lobby lounge and private study rooms, including one that must be reserved ahead.
cards.source_title: One Palace Road Study Map | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Private-study-room use and after-hours access are subject to the building map’s instructions and reservation rules.

cards.title: Share a Meal at Bartol
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop — Residence Campus
cards.notes: Meet over a meal at Bartol, then compare classes, clubs, and plans for the week; choose options that work for your dietary needs before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A residence-campus meal stop built for catching up.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes Bartol Dining Hall as its all-you-care-to-eat dining facility on the residence campus, with vegetarian options, salad bars, sautés, pizza, and smoothies.
cards.access_notes: Dining is paid through an applicable meal plan or other offered payment option; check current menu and hours first.

cards.title: Take a Movement Break at Holmes
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop — 331 Brookline Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a low-key workout, lap swim, or indoor-track visit around your access privileges, then save the recreation schedule for future fitness classes.
cards.short_summary: A practical recreation stop on the Residence Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons identifies the Holmes Sports Center as a 60,000-square-foot facility with a swimming pool, cardio equipment, and hardwood courts for students and members.
cards.access_notes: Student or member access applies; verify facility and lap-swim availability before heading over.

cards.title: Use Your Simmons ID at the Gardner
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop — 25 Evans Way, beside the Academic Campus
cards.notes: Reserve a timed entry, bring your Simmons ID, and give yourself time to move through the galleries without treating the visit like a rushed checklist.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum visit available to Simmons students with ID.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ official Boston guide states that Simmons students receive free admission to the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum by showing their Simmons ID.
cards.source_title: The Official Simmons Guide to Boston | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: The museum recommends advanced timed tickets; bring a current Simmons ID for the stated free-admission benefit.

cards.title: Finish with Free Contemporary Art at MAAM
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop — 621 Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve a time slot, explore the current galleries, and end the weekend by discussing one work that caught your attention before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary-art stop near the Longwood Medical Green Line station.
cards.evidence_claim: MassArt Art Museum identifies itself as Boston’s only free museum of contemporary art and asks visitors to reserve tickets in advance.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; reserve in advance and check current open days before leaving campus.
